transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what finally made me come in is my eating has gotten kind of... unpredictable. For months now, my appetite’s been all over the place. Some evenings I just skip dinner and then notice my clothes are looser, like I’m losing weight without trying. Other nights I’ll stand in the kitchen and end up picking at crackers or cereal because making an actual meal for just me feels pointless.

I mean, I work around people all day, so you’d think I’d be better at noticing this stuff in myself, but somehow it’s different when it’s you.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that activities you once found interesting or pleasurable feel like a chore?

Yeah… I have noticed that. I still do the things, sort of. Like I’ll go out to water the garden because the tomatoes won’t wait for me to feel inspired, you know? And I used to actually enjoy that—checking the leaves, moving things around, fussing over it. Lately I’m just standing there with the hose, kind of blank, doing it because it needs doing.

Same with book club. I’ll show up, and everyone’s talking about the book and someone’s brought those little lemon cookies—Linda always does that, she’s very proud of them—and I just sit there thinking I should be enjoying this. But it feels flat. Sometimes I leave early, or I don’t even start the book in the first place. It’s not that I hate any of it. It just feels like a chore now.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most days, or that your mood is consistently low even when there’s no clear reason for it?

I’m… not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I know what the word means, obviously, and I ask clients about mood all the time, which almost makes it harder to answer for myself.

Some days I’m just sort of quiet or heavy, but then I’ll get distracted by work or some errand—last week I spent twenty minutes trying to find the right kind of mulch at the garden center, and the cashier was telling me about her dahlias, and I remember thinking, “Well, I’m functioning, right?” So… I don’t know if it’s most days or just when I stop moving.

It’s not like there’s always a clear reason, but I have a hard time separating mood from everything else. I guess I’ve noticed something feels off, but I can’t neatly say, yes, I feel down every day.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or that you have less energy than usual, even after getting enough rest?

Yes… I think so. Even when my caseload isn’t especially awful, I still feel like I’m dragging myself through the hospital. Like my body is heavier than it should be.

And then I get home and it’s ridiculous—I’ll have good intentions, like I’ll cook something decent, or stretch because my back’s been tight, or text someone back. But I’ll sit down for a minute and suddenly all of that feels like too much. I’ll think, “Just answer the message, it’s not hard,” and then I don’t. So yes, less energy, I guess. Even when I should have enough left.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not good enough even when there’s no real reason for it?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t walk around thinking, “I’m worthless,” exactly. That feels too dramatic. But I do catch myself replaying the marriage a lot, like I’m going back over a chart after something went wrong, looking for the missed sign.

I’ll be washing a mug or pulling weeds and suddenly I’m thinking, maybe I failed at something really basic. Like being a wife, or being… I don’t know, easy to stay with. And then the rational part of me says relationships are complicated, nobody gets graded on them like an exam. But that doesn’t always stop the loop.

It’s funny, because with clients I’d never frame it that way. I’d be much kinder. But with myself, it turns into this quiet blame thing. Not all the time, but more than I’d like.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that nothing seems to make you feel good anymore?

Yeah… that one’s harder to dodge, I guess. I still do the things, or I try to. Like the garden—I’ll go out with the watering can, and then I’m just standing there thinking the tomatoes look a little sad, and I should probably stake them better, and then I remember my neighbor’s ridiculous zucchini situation last summer—

Sorry. The point is, it used to feel good. Calming, or satisfying. Now a lot of the time it’s just… a task.

Same with book club. I’ll show up because I said I would, and everyone’s talking and laughing, and I’m following along, mostly, but it feels sort of flat. Like I’m watching it instead of being in it. Sometimes I leave early, or I don’t even start the thing I thought I wanted to do. So yes, I think I’m not getting the same pleasure from things I used to.
Would you say that these low feelings or this lack of enjoyment happen on most days, even if they vary in intensity?

Most days, yes… though it’s not always the same level. Some days I can sort of fake it better, I guess.

I still do the things I used to like—water the garden, go to book club if I’ve already promised I’d come. But a lot of the time it feels flat, like I’m just completing the step because it’s on the list. And then I’ll leave early, or I’ll stand in the kitchen thinking I should go outside and just… not start.

It’s strange because nothing dramatic is happening in that moment. The watering can is there, the book is on the table, everyone at book club is perfectly nice. It just doesn’t land the way it used to.
Would you say that your low mood or not feeling pleasure in things happens on most days, and if so, does it usually last throughout the day, nearly every day?

Most days, yes… or, I mean, it feels like that. Not every single minute, but it hangs around a lot.

I’ll still do the things I used to love, like watering the garden, or I’ll show up to book club because I said I would. And then I’m there, but it just feels flat. Like I’m going through the motions. Sometimes I end up leaving early, or I don’t even get started in the first place.

The garden is funny because I used to lose track of time out there, fussing over little things, and now I’ll stand there with the hose and think, “Okay, I guess this needs water,” and that’s it. So… yes, it’s most days, and it lasts enough of the day that I notice it.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower in a way I could point to, or being unable to sit still.

I mean, I do sometimes sort of… linger over things, like I’ll stand in the kitchen and forget what I meant to grab, but that might just be me being distracted. My mother used to do that thing where she’d walk into a room and blame the doorway for stealing her thoughts—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

So, no, I don’t think I’ve noticed a big change with moving slowly or feeling physically restless. At least not enough that I’d know to call it that.
Would you say that your low mood or lack of enjoyment in things has been present most of the time, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yes… most of the time, I think so. I mean, I keep trying to do the normal things so it doesn’t look like I’ve stopped living my life or anything.

Like I still water the garden, or I’ll go to book club if I told them I’d be there, but it’s not the same. It’s sort of like checking a box. And sometimes I leave early, or I just stand there thinking I should start and then I don’t. My neighbor has this ridiculous tomato plant that’s somehow doing better than mine even though she barely touches it—sorry, that’s not really the point.

The point is, yes, it’s been there most days. That flat feeling. For at least the last couple weeks, yes.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like the garden or book club, even if it’s just for a little while?

Completely lost interest… I don’t know if I’d say completely, because I still do show up sometimes. Like, I’ll water the garden because it needs doing, or I’ll go to book club because I said I would and I don’t want to be rude.

But it feels flat most of the time. Like I’m there, but I’m not really getting anything from it. Sometimes I leave book club early, or with the garden I’ll just sort of stand there and not really start. I used to fuss over the plants and enjoy it, and now it’s more like… checking a chore off a list.
Would you say that you feel depressed or down most of the time, nearly every day, even if it’s not extremely intense?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I do feel down a lot, but “most of the time, nearly every day” makes me start second-guessing myself, like I should be keeping a chart or something.

Some days I can get through things and seem fine, at least from the outside. Other times it’s just sort of sitting there in the background. My old supervisor used to say people can function and still not be okay—she had this mug with a terrible quote on it, actually—but sorry, I’m wandering.

I guess I know I haven’t felt like myself, but I’m not sure I can say it neatly the way you asked.
Would you say that you’ve experienced days where you feel no interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even for a period of time?

Yes… yes, I have. I mean, I still do the things sometimes, like watering the garden or going to book club, but it’s more like I’m just moving through the motions.

I’ll stand there with the hose and not really care about the plants the way I used to, or I’ll get to book club and realize I’m just waiting for it to be over. Sometimes I leave early. Other times I don’t even really get started, which is silly because it’s not like watering a garden is complicated.

So yes, there are definitely days where there’s just no real pleasure in it. It all feels kind of flat.
Would you say that you've felt a loss of energy or fatigue nearly every day for at least the past two weeks?

Yes, I think so. I mean, I’m tired a lot, even when my caseload isn’t especially awful. I’ll be walking through the hospital and it feels like I’m dragging my whole body around, which sounds dramatic, but that’s how it feels.

And then I get home and I’m just… done. Too tired to cook properly, or stretch, or even answer messages from people. I’ll see them on my phone and think, “I’ll do it in a minute,” and then suddenly it’s much later. So, yes, it’s been pretty consistent.
Would you say that your changes in appetite or weight have been happening nearly every day for at least the past two weeks?

Yes, that’s actually one of the things that finally made me make the appointment. My appetite has been… not steady at all. For months, really, there are stretches where I’ll just skip dinner without meaning to, and then I notice my clothes are looser or the scale is down, and I didn’t try to lose weight.

And then other nights I’ll sort of stand in the kitchen and end up eating crackers or a bowl of cereal, not because I want it exactly, but because cooking for just me feels… pointless. I know that sounds a little silly, because I used to be pretty decent about making actual meals. I even had this one soup recipe I’d make on Sundays—but sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So yes, the appetite and weight changes have been happening pretty regularly, not just once or twice.

Yes, I think so. I mean, I’m tired a lot, even when my caseload isn’t especially awful. I’ll be walking through the hospital and it feels like I’m dragging my whole body around, which sounds dramatic, but that’s how it feels.

And then I get home and I’m just… done. Too tired to cook properly, or stretch, or even answer messages from people. I’ll see them on my phone and think, “I’ll do it in a minute,” and then suddenly it’s much later. So, yes, it’s been pretty consistent.

inference.note: The patient has confirmed persistent low mood, loss of interest and pleasure in previously enjoyed activities, fatigue, and reduced energy nearly every day for at least the past two weeks. These findings support the presence of a major depressive episode. However, the duration of the current episode (whether it meets criteria for a single episode versus recurrent depressive disorder) has not yet been fully clarified, so both F32 and F33 codes remain under consideration. Further clarification is needed to determine if this is a single episode (F32) or recurrent (F33), and its severity.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant change in appetite or weight nearly every day for at least the past two weeks.
doctor.question: Would you say that your changes in appetite or weight have been happening nearly every day for at least the past two weeks?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What finally made me come in is that my appetite has been all over the place for months, with stretches where I skip dinner and lose weight without trying and other nights when I pick at crackers or cereal just because cooking for myself feels pointless.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about changes in appetite or weight and whether they have been occurring nearly every day for at least two weeks.

patient.answer:
Yes, that’s actually one of the things that finally made me make the appointment. My appetite has been… not steady at all. For months, really, there are stretches where I’ll just skip dinner without meaning to, and then I notice my clothes are looser or the scale is down, and I didn’t try to lose weight.

And then other nights I’ll sort of stand in the kitchen and end up eating crackers or a bowl of cereal, not because I want it exactly, but because cooking for just me feels… pointless. I know that sounds a little silly, because I used to be pretty decent about making actual meals. I even had this one soup recipe I’d make on Sundays—but sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So yes, the appetite and weight changes have been happening pretty regularly, not just once or twice.
